name: Collocational Range
description: Measures the range and diversity of lexical collocations — AI text often uses narrower collocational patterns.
mechanism:
This method detects AI-generated text by measuring the breadth and diversity of word combinations used. While individual collocations may be correct, AI text tends to rely on a narrower set of word pairings than human writing:

1. **Collocational Type-Token Ratio**: The method extracts all significant collocations (bigrams with PMI > 2.0 from COCA reference) and computes the collocational type-token ratio (CTTR) — the number of unique collocation types divided by total collocation tokens. Human text shows CTTR of 0.75–0.90 (most collocations are used only once); AI text shows CTTR of 0.55–0.70 (more repetition of the same word combinations). Additionally, the method computes the collocational hapax ratio — proportion of collocations appearing exactly once. Human: 0.65–0.80; AI: 0.45–0.60. High repetition of collocations suggests the model is drawing from a limited set of preferred combinations.

2. **Collocational Span Analysis**: For each content word, the method measures its collocational span — the number of distinct words it collocates with in the text. Using a window of ±4 words, each noun, verb, and adjective is profiled: (a) mean span — average number of distinct collocates per content word. Human text: 2.5–4.0 collocates per word; AI text: 1.5–2.5. (b) Span distribution — human text shows a power-law distribution (most words have few collocates, a few words have many); AI text shows a more uniform distribution with fewer high-span words. (c) Novel collocations — word pairs not found in the top-1000 collocations for either word in the reference corpus. Human text: 15–25% novel collocations; AI text: 5–12%. The span analysis reveals whether the text explores the full collocational potential of its vocabulary or sticks to safe, high-frequency combinations.

3. **Semantic Field Collocational Coverage**: The method groups words into semantic fields (using WordNet domains or USAS semantic tags) and measures collocational diversity within each field. For example, in the "cooking" semantic field, human text might use: "simmer gently", "reduce the sauce", "fold in the eggs", "a pinch of salt" — diverse collocations drawn from specialized knowledge. AI text in the same field tends to use fewer, more generic collocations: "cook the food", "add the ingredients", "prepare the meal". The method computes: (a) within-field collocational entropy — human: H > 3.0 bits; AI: H < 2.5 bits, (b) cross-field collocational consistency — whether the writer uses equally diverse collocations across topics or shows expertise in some fields and generic language in others. Human text usually shows uneven expertise; AI shows uniform mediocrity.

4. **Collocational Creativity Index**: The method specifically measures creative or unexpected word combinations that signal genuine language mastery: (a) low-PMI acceptable collocations — word pairs with PMI < 1.5 that are nonetheless semantically coherent (creative metaphors, novel descriptions). Human text: 5–10% of collocations; AI text: 1–3%. (b) Register-crossing collocations — combining formal and informal collocates within a sentence for stylistic effect ("The committee conducted a thorough deep-dive"). Human text: 1–3 per 1000 words; AI text: < 0.5. (c) Collocational deviation — deliberately violating conventional collocations for emphasis ("she heavily whispered" — unusual but expressive). Human creative writing: 2–5 per 1000 words; AI text: < 0.5. The creativity index combines these measures into a composite score (0–1 scale): human text averages 0.55–0.75; AI text averages 0.20–0.40.
parameters:
PMI reference corpus: COCA (560M words)
PMI threshold for significant collocations: > 2.0
Collocational window: ±4 words
CTTR human: 0.75–0.90
CTTR AI: 0.55–0.70
Mean span human: 2.5–4.0 collocates/word
Mean span AI: 1.5–2.5
Novel collocation human: 15–25%
Novel collocation AI: 5–12%
Creativity index human: 0.55–0.75
Minimum text length: 300 words
accuracy: 77–86% accuracy detecting AI-generated text via collocational range analysis. CTTR achieves AUC of 0.83. Semantic field coverage adds 3–4% improvement. Creativity index provides F1-score of 0.81. Performance best for creative and editorial text; lower for technical text with standardized collocations.
source: Hoey, M. (2005). Lexical Priming: A New Theory of Words and Language. Routledge.
useCase: Detecting AI-generated articles through narrow collocational patterns. Evaluating vocabulary richness beyond simple word diversity. Identifying AI-written creative content through collocational predictability. Analyzing writing style depth through combinatorial variety.
strengths:
• Captures a dimension of language use invisible to simple vocabulary metrics
• Collocational span reveals genuine word mastery vs. surface knowledge
• Semantic field analysis detects domain-specific language quality
• Creativity index targets the most distinctive human writing feature
• Complementary to collocational error detection
limitations:
• Requires reference corpus for PMI and span baseline calculations
• Technical and formulaic writing naturally has narrower collocational range
• Very short texts provide insufficient collocation data
• Domain-specific jargon may produce low-PMI collocations that are appropriate
• Advanced AI models are generating more diverse collocations

references.title: Hoey, M. — Lexical Priming: A New Theory of Words and Language (Routledge 2005)
Sinclair, J. — Corpus, Concordance, Collocation (Oxford University Press 1991)
